  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "Use Welch's ANOVA if variance homogeneity is violated due to unequal group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Bright Visual Only n=3323)",
    "For Success (binary: 0/1), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA, as ANOVA assumptions are violated for binary outcomes",
    "Include Mouse as a random effect in mixed-effects models to account for repeated measures across 8 mice, given substantial mouse-level clustering (SC21LM: 10986 trials, SC11LM: 7233 trials)",
    "Report effect sizes (eta-squared or partial eta-squared) for all significant ANOVA results"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "Apply Tukey's HSD for pairwise comparisons if variances are homogeneous and sample sizes balanced",
    "Use Games-Howell post-hoc tests if Welch's ANOVA indicates heteroscedasticity, given extreme imbalance between Combined (48846) and Bright Visual Only (3323)",
    "For Success analyzed via logistic regression, use pairwise z-tests with Bonferroni correction or marginal means comparisons",
    "Focus post-hoc comparisons on Combined vs single-modality conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and all conditions vs Sham baseline",
    "Report 95% confidence intervals for all pairwise differences"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Bonferroni correction across the 5 ANOVA models (one per response variable), yielding family-wise alpha = 0.05/5 = 0.01 per test; within each ANOVA, use Tukey or Games-Howell to control family-wise error for the 10 pairwise comparisons among 5 paradigms",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression or ordinal regression if stimulation paradigm has natural ordering; otherwise random forest or gradient boosting classifier for categorical response with 5 unordered classes. Given the extreme class imbalance (Combined: 48846/76655 = 63.7% vs Bright Visual Only: 3323/76655 = 4.3%), use class-weighted loss functions or resampling (SMOTE) to prevent trivial prediction of majority class. Alternative: ordinal encoding if paradigms represent intensity (Sham < Dim Visual < Bright Visual < ICMS Only < Combined) and proportional odds model. Cross-validate with stratified k-fold to preserve class distribution. Do NOT use ordinary linear regression—stimulation paradigm is categorical with no natural metric spacing.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check normality of residuals with Shapiro-Wilk tests and Q-Q plots; consider log-transformation for Time-to-Target given max=201.39 vs mean=2.81 indicating right skew",
    "Test homogeneity of variance with Levene's test; expect violation due to 14.7x sample size ratio between largest and smallest groups",
    "Assess independence assumption via examination of Mouse clustering; likely violated requiring mixed-effects or clustered standard errors",
    "For multinomial logistic regression, check IIA (Independence of Irrelevant Alternatives) with Hausman-McFadden test",
    "Evaluate multicollinearity among predictors (Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD may correlate) using VIF < 5 threshold",
    "Verify no perfect separation in logistic models given binary Success outcome"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, higher Average Speed, lower AD) compared to single-modality conditions based on multisensory integration literature",
    "ICMS Only expected to outperform visual-only conditions given direct cortical engagement",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance, serving as baseline for effect size estimation",
    "Dim Visual Only vs Bright Visual Only comparison may reveal intensity-dependent effects or ceiling effects",
    "Large sample size (n=76655) will yield statistically significant differences even for small effect sizes; emphasize practical significance via Cohen's d or eta-squared",
    "AD (angular dispersion) expected to inversely correlate with Path Efficiency and Success, serving as trajectory straightness indicator"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance in Stim Paradigm (Combined 63.7% vs Bright Visual Only 4.3%) reduces power for comparisons involving rare conditions and biases predictive models toward majority class",
    "Mouse-level clustering unaccounted for in standard ANOVA inflates Type I error; mixed-effects models required but may converge poorly with extreme imbalance",
    "Success is binary but treated as continuous in naive ANOVA; logistic or beta regression more appropriate",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme range (min=0.000928, max=29.82, mean=0.47) suggesting outliers or calculation artifacts that may violate normality",
    "No temporal information (trial order, learning effects) available in current data view; cannot assess within-session or across-session performance changes",
    "Temperature=0.25 and prompt template suggest LLM-generated labels; potential measurement error in paradigm assignment unverifiable from summary data",
    "Replication=3 indicates this is one of multiple runs; cross-run validation needed for generalizability"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression with Mouse as random intercept, Stim Paradigm as response, and all five performance variables as predictors, using class weights to address imbalance. Perform 5-fold stratified cross-validation and report macro-averaged F1 and per-class precision/recall. Supplement with permutation-based variable importance to identify which performance metrics most discriminate paradigms. Finally, conduct equivalence testing (TOST) for non-significant pairwise comparisons to distinguish absence of evidence from evidence of absence."
}
